memory_update.text: Manhattan Associates is the cleanest underfollowed public pure-play for omnichannel order orchestration and warehouse execution.
SPS Commerce is a second underfollowed public exposure because it monetizes retailer-supplier trading-partner complexity rather than consumer demand directly.
Consumer-theme screens can miss enterprise software vendors that sit one step upstream from omnichannel retail fulfillment; the useful discovery lane is mid-cap software, not only consumer brands.

MANH is the reference benchmark for omnichannel order management, warehouse management, WES, TMS, and retail fulfillment orchestration; useful for validating product taxonomy and customer workflow relevance.

SPSC is an underfollowed consumer-retail supply-chain network candidate: less obvious than OMS/WMS vendors but exposed to retailer-supplier onboarding, EDI, product/order visibility, and trading-partner automation.

DSGX is an underfollowed second-order ecommerce fulfillment and logistics execution candidate through ecommerce shipping, routing, mobile, telematics, trade compliance, carrier connectivity, and logistics-network data.

ZBRA should be tracked as a physical data-capture infrastructure supplier for omnichannel execution, not as a pure software vendor; evidence needs retail/ecommerce end-market growth, RFID adoption, and software attach-rate confirmation.

E2open fits the node conceptually but appears no longer suitable for the US-listed universe after WiseTech acquisition/delisting; consider WiseTech only if non-US listings are allowed in a later pass.
MANH is the strongest reference comp for omnichannel order orchestration and supply-chain execution software; classify as reference rather than hidden alpha unless valuation/coverage resets.
SPSC is a strong underfollowed lane candidate: retail supply-chain network, partner connectivity, omnichannel adoption, and compliance rails create indirect exposure to consumer ecommerce complexity.

DSGX is a plausible underfollowed mid-cap candidate because transportation management, routing, home delivery, final-mile, and ecommerce inventory capabilities sit one layer away from retail order orchestration.
TCYSF/Tecsys should remain a speculative shadow candidate pending verification of US investability, liquidity, market cap, and retail/ecommerce revenue materiality.

E2open and Logility screen well for supply-chain software but appear no longer independently publicly listed after 2025 acquisitions; remove from active US-listed universe while keeping as private-market comp signals.

MANH is the reference public pure-play for omnichannel order orchestration, WMS, TMS, labor, inventory, and retail commerce execution; include as context but do not let it crowd out smaller discovery names.

SPSC is a strong underfollowed candidate for the retail trading-partner connectivity layer; it may benefit from retailer-mandated supplier compliance and omnichannel complexity even though it is not a classic OMS/WMS vendor.

DSGX offers adjacent exposure through logistics, routing, inventory, and ecommerce fulfillment software; verify ecommerce-specific revenue and whether freight/logistics cyclicality dilutes the retail fulfillment thesis.

GDYN is a speculative_shadow candidate for implementation capacity around Blue Yonder OMS/WMS/TMS and composable commerce projects; require evidence of material revenue from these partnerships before promotion.

Several seemingly relevant node assets are private or no longer US-listed, including Blue Yonder, OneRail, Logility after Aptean transaction, and E2open after WiseTech acquisition; this reduces the available pure-play public universe and increases the need to map adjacent public beneficiaries.

node: Omnichannel order management, warehouse execution, and fulfillment orchestration software
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This node expands into a small set of public software vendors that sit inside retailer fulfillment flows, plus a large omnichannel retailer as customer-context anchor. The cleanest underfollowed public exposures are Manhattan Associates, SPS Commerce, and Descartes Systems Group; Walmart is included as a high-attention demand-side anchor because its omnichannel fulfillment model illustrates why this software layer matters. Expanded the universe around scarce, deeply embedded omnichannel and fulfillment-execution software. The cleanest reference name is Manhattan Associates, but the underfollowed lane includes SPS Commerce and Descartes, which sit one step away from obvious consumer retail demand through retail trading networks, logistics execution, ecommerce shipping, routing, and fulfillment data flows. Zebra is included as a second-order infrastructure provider because order orchestration systems depend on frontline barcode/RFID/mobile-computing data capture in stores, warehouses, yards, and delivery workflows. E2open was considered but is flagged as a coverage gap rather than a candidate because it appears to have been acquired/delisted in 2025. Expanded the universe around omnichannel order orchestration and supply-chain execution software. The cleanest US-listed exposure remains Manhattan Associates as the reference comp, but the underfollowed lane includes SPS Commerce, Descartes Systems Group, and OTC-listed Tecsys as smaller or less consumer-obvious assets tied to retail supply-chain networks, transportation/logistics execution, inventory visibility, WMS, and fulfil
